mcqs.q: The basic premise of this topic is that technology:
opts: Improves the quality of medical care and patient safety
mcqs.explain: The basic premise is that technology improves the quality of medical care and patient safety.

mcqs.q: The IOM report 'To Err is Human' estimated that:
opts: Many inpatients die every year due to preventable errors
No patients are harmed by errors
mcqs.explain: The IOM report 'To Err is Human' estimated that many inpatients die every year due to preventable errors, describing an 'era of Brownian motion in health care.'

mcqs.q: A key IOM recommendation was to:
opts: Create a national information infrastructure and eliminate handwritten notes
mcqs.explain: The IOM recommended creating a national information infrastructure to improve care/research, with a goal of eliminating handwritten notes.

mcqs.q: Prescribing antibiotics for a viral infection is an example of which error category?
mcqs.explain: Overuse is the widespread use of a treatment where not indicated — e.g. antibiotics for viral infections.

mcqs.q: Failing to give vaccines, cancer screening or post-MI beta-blockers is:
mcqs.explain: Underuse is the failure to provide indicated care, e.g. vaccines, cancer screening or beta-blockers after a heart attack.

mcqs.q: 'Failure to rescue' as a safety issue means:
opts: Not recognizing and treating a deteriorating patient
mcqs.explain: Failure to rescue is not recognizing and treating a deteriorating patient — one of the six leading safety/quality issues.

mcqs.q: Which is a recognised BARRIER to improving patient safety through technology?
opts: Organizational, financial, privacy and security concerns
mcqs.explain: Barriers include organizational, financial, trained HIT workforce, privacy, security, behavioral and error-reporting issues.

mcqs.q: Why does SECURITY act as a barrier to technology adoption?
opts: Major identity-theft episodes have alarmed patients and slowed EHR adoption
mcqs.explain: Several major episodes of identity theft alarmed patients/staff and contributed to the slow adoption of EHRs and other technologies.

mcqs.q: The 'behavioral' barrier to safety technology refers to:
opts: Lack of use of computerized physician order entry (CPOE)
mcqs.explain: The behavioral barrier is the lack of use of computerized physician order entry (CPOE).

mcqs.q: A limitation of the Patient Safety and Quality Improvement Act is that:
opts: There is no definition of 'error' and data needs the physician's permission
mcqs.explain: The Act is limited because there is no definition of 'error', and data can only be used in a criminal case and with the physician's permission.

mcqs.q: To improve the accuracy of patient IDENTIFICATION, the technology with most potential is:
mcqs.explain: Improving the accuracy of patient identification has potential for bar coding.

mcqs.q: To improve COMMUNICATION among caregivers, one can:
opts: Expedite critical results via cell phones or VoIP
mcqs.explain: Communication can be improved by expediting critical test results using cell phones or VoIP, plus portals, telemedicine and health information organizations.

mcqs.q: The MOST important patient-safety area impacted by healthcare IT is:
mcqs.explain: Medication error reduction remains the most important patient safety area impacted by healthcare IT.

mcqs.q: The 'five rights' before medication administration are:
opts: Right drug, right patient, right dosage, right route, right time
Right doctor, room, day, nurse, bed
Right colour, taste, smell, size, shape
Right fee, form, file, fax, phone
mcqs.explain: The five rights are: right drug, right patient, right dosage, right route and right time.

mcqs.q: Computerized physician order entry (CPOE) primarily:
opts: Reduces medication errors by processing orders electronically
mcqs.explain: CPOE (inpatient and outpatient) electronically processes orders and reduces medication errors, costs and variation of care.

mcqs.q: Automated inpatient medication dispensing devices work most like:
opts: ATM machines — communicating with pharmacy computers and keeping records
mcqs.explain: Like ATM machines, these devices communicate with pharmacy computers, dispense stocked medications and keep medication records.

mcqs.q: The EMMA home medication management system is mainly for:
opts: The elderly at home, with visual/audible reminders and compliance monitoring
mcqs.explain: EMMA is mainly for the elderly at home; it is connected to the pharmacy via the Internet to monitor compliance, adjust doses and give visual/audible alerts.

mcqs.q: Pharmacy dispensing robots are especially helpful when there is:
opts: A shortage of pharmacists or staff
mcqs.explain: Robots are helpful during pharmacist/staff shortages, giving pharmacists a supervisory role; prescriptions are checked by both the EHR and the pharmacist.

mcqs.q: An advantage of the electronic medication administration record (eMAR) is:
opts: No need to search for the patient's chart to see their medications
Only the pharmacist can see it
mcqs.explain: With eMAR there is no need to search for the patient's chart; the application is available to nurses and physicians making rounds.

mcqs.q: 'Smart' IV infusion pumps include a feature known as a:
mcqs.explain: Smart pumps deliver correct IV drug amounts and, with drug libraries and alerts that the dose differs from guidelines, provide a 'dose error reduction system' (DERS).

mcqs.q: An advantage of RFID over standard bar codes is that RFID tags:
opts: Can be read if wet or through clothing and can track patients
Require a direct laser line of sight
mcqs.explain: RFID tags can be read if wet or through clothing (better for blood/IV bags) and can track patients with an active tag giving location and time.

mcqs.q: Medication errors are MORE likely to occur when:
opts: Patients move between hospitals, physicians or floors
mcqs.explain: Errors are more likely when patients move hospital-to-hospital, physician-to-physician or floor-to-floor; a shared health information organization makes reconciliation electronic.

mcqs.q: Electronic prescribing (eRx) is available as:
opts: Standalone software OR integrated into an EHR
mcqs.explain: E-prescribing comes in two modes: a standalone software program (smartphone/computer/web) or eRx integrated into an electronic health record.

mcqs.q: The Johns Hopkins paediatric TPN calculator is an example of how which technology reduces errors?
mcqs.explain: Johns Hopkins created a web-based paediatric total parenteral (IV) nutrition (TPN) calculator that reduced medication errors.

saqs.q: List the three categories of medical errors with an example of each.
saqs.a: Overuse (antibiotics for viral infections), underuse (vaccines, beta-blockers post-MI), and misuse (TB not given the four recommended drugs initially).

saqs.q: List the six leading safety/quality issues.
saqs.a: Severe infection, post-operative respiratory failure, bed sores, blood clots, hospital-acquired infections, and failure to rescue.

saqs.q: List the barriers to improving patient safety through technology.
saqs.a: Organizational, financial, trained HIT workforce, privacy, security, behavioral, and error reporting.

saqs.q: List the health goals that have IT implications.
saqs.a: 1) Improve accuracy of patient identification (bar coding); 2) improve communication among caregivers (VoIP, portals, telemedicine); 3) improve medication safety; 4) accurately reconcile medications across the continuum of care.

saqs.q: State the 'five rights' of medication administration.
saqs.a: Right drug, right patient, right dosage, right route, right time.

saqs.q: List technologies that can decrease medication errors.
saqs.a: CPOE, automated dispensing devices, home systems (EMMA), pharmacy robots, eMAR, smart IV pumps, calculators, bar-coding/RFID, medication reconciliation, and e-prescribing.

saqs.q: Describe EMMA and the advantages of RFID.
saqs.a: EMMA is a home medication-management device for the elderly, connected to the pharmacy via the Internet to monitor compliance and give visual/audible alerts. RFID tags can be read when wet or through clothing and can track patients (a 16-digit chip links to the web record).
